terms.gloss: a choosing, a careful selection; discernment
evidence: Caesar in Cic. Brut. 253: verbōrum dīlēctum orīginem esse ēloquentiae
Cic. Off. 1.49: acceptōrum autem beneficiōrum sunt dīlēctūs habendī
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives both spellings (dīlēctus in many editions, after the best manuscripts); sine dēlēctū, without discrimination. Also the levy of soldiers. Making a choice is usually the verb, ēligere (see choose).
Once in Cicero, then in Quintilian, Tacitus and other imperial prose (Lewis & Short); in Christian Latin the election of the faithful.

phrases.english: that the choice of words is the origin of eloquence

phrases.latin: Acceptōrum autem beneficiōrum sunt dīlēctūs habendī
phrases.english: But among favours received we must make distinctions

sources: Lewis & Short: delectus · Lewis & Short: electio
